urate.title: {Plural} and urate stones
urate.text: {Plural} are prone to urate bladder stones, and Merck's prevention is a low-purine diet. Liver and other organ meats are high in purine; eggs and vegetables are low (VCA). We never list organ meats as something to share. {name} is {ageText}, {lb} lb{kcalClause}. Ask your vet about a low-purine food.

pancreatitis_prone.title: {Plural} and pancreatitis
pancreatitis_prone.text: {Plural} are dramatically overrepresented among dogs with pancreatitis (Merck), and very high blood triglycerides raise the risk. Most Schnauzers do fine on a normal diet; ask your vet to check triglycerides at check-ups. For dogs being treated for pancreatitis, Merck's diet is less than 20 g fat per 1,000 kcal. That is a treatment diet your vet would set, not a rule for every Schnauzer. If {name} is ever diagnosed, add Pancreatitis under restrictions and extras pause. {name} is {ageText}, {lb} lb{kcalClause}. Ask your vet.

copper_prone.title: {Plural} and copper
copper_prone.text: {Plural} are among the breeds prone to copper build-up in the liver (Cornell). Most dogs never have a problem; ask your vet about a copper check at {name}'s next visit. If a vet ever puts {name} on a low-copper diet, Cornell's list is: no organ meats, no shellfish, no mushrooms, fewer green leafy vegetables. Add it under restrictions here and extras pause until you say otherwise. Ask your vet.

growth_large.title: A growing {label}
growth_large.text: {name} is {monthsText}. Large-breed puppies stay on puppy food until 12 to 18 months; ask your vet which. Keep {name} trim (body condition 4 to 5 of 9) and follow the growth chart at check-ups. Ask your vet.

merck_urolithiasis_dogs.title: Urolithiasis in Dogs
merck_urolithiasis_dogs.quote: A mutation of a gene that encodes for a uric acid transporter (SLC2A9) has been found in Dalmatians with hyperuricosuria. Feeding a low-purine diet with or without supplemental potassium citrate to alkalinize the urine discourages the formation of new stones.

vca_dalmatian.title: Dalmatian
vca_dalmatian.quote: Liver and other organ meats are high in purine and should be avoided in these dogs. Eggs and vegetables are low in purine.

merck_pancreatitis.title: Pancreatitis in Dogs and Cats
merck_pancreatitis.quote: Miniature Schnauzers have been reported to be dramatically overrepresented. In dogs, feeding a low-fat diet (ie, less than 20 g fat/1,000 kcal) is crucial for treatment success.

jvim_schnauzer_2020.title: Effect of a low-fat diet on serum triglyceride and cholesterol concentrations and lipoprotein profiles in Miniature Schnauzers with hypertriglyceridemia
jvim_schnauzer_2020.quote: The most commonly recommended initial approach in the management of hypertriglyceridemia is the use of a low-fat diet.

cornell_copper.title: Copper hepatopathy and dietary management
cornell_copper.quote: Labrador Retriever, Doberman Pinscher, Bedlington Terrier, and West Highland White are examples of highly prone breeds. No organ meats. No shellfish. No mushrooms. Fewer green leafy vegetables.

tufts_growth_2022.title: Growth guide: keeping your puppy on the right track
tufts_growth_2022.quote: But PLEASE don't change to an adult food before 12 months of age in small, medium, or large-sized breeds

wsava_bcs_dog.title: Body Condition Score (dog)
wsava_bcs_dog.quote: Body condition score chart, 9-point scale; ideal 4 to 5.
